meta.title: Radix Infrastructure
meta.description: A complete breakdown of the Radix full-stack technical infrastructure: from the ledger and consensus layers to DeFi, identity and developer tooling.

hero.title: Infrastructure
hero.description: Radix was built from scratch, not forked from Ethereum or Bitcoin, with a single purpose: to be the global base layer for finance. Explore every technical layer of the stack below.

ledger.title: Ledger & Storage
ledger.subtitle: The Ground of the Network
ledger.description: The physical foundation where all data resides. Radix does not use a traditional blockchain; instead it uses a massively pre-sharded distributed ledger designed for infinite parallelism.

global_ledger.title: Radix Global Ledger
global_ledger.description: An immense distributed ledger pre-sharded from day one into 2²⁵⁶ shards. It is the infinite canvas on which every asset, identity and smart component exists.

substate_model.title: Substate Model
substate_model.description: Every asset, resource and smart component is an independent "substate" on the ledger, enabling fully parallel processing of interactions that touch different parts of the ledger.

jmt.title: Jellyfish Merkle Tree (JMT)
jmt.description: The underlying cryptographic data structure that stores and verifies all substates with ultra-fast read/write performance, enabling cryptographic proofs of any ledger state.

consensus.title: Network & Consensus
consensus.subtitle: The Muscle and the Scalability
consensus.description: This layer dictates how validator nodes agree on ledger updates. Cerberus and Hyperscale together deliver linear scalability: the more nodes, the more throughput: without bottlenecks.

cerberus.title: Cerberus (Braided Consensus)
cerberus.description: The native consensus algorithm that enables atomic transactions spanning multiple shards simultaneously. A complex operation either executes in full or is rolled back entirely: no partial failures.

hyperscale.title: Hyperscale Architecture
hyperscale.description: The network topology and parallelisation layer that allows Cerberus to scale horizontally. Adding validator nodes directly increases transactions per second (TPS) without any ceiling.

nodes.title: Validator, Full & Archive Nodes
nodes.description: Decentralised physical servers that run Cerberus, secure the network via XRD staking, process transaction batches and store the complete ledger history for auditability.

execution.title: Execution & Programming
execution.subtitle: The Brain
execution.description: The environment where smart logic is built and run. Radix Engine's asset-oriented model treats tokens as physical resources: they cannot disappear or be duplicated by a code bug.

radix_engine.title: Radix Engine v2
radix_engine.description: The Virtual Machine of the network. It is an "Asset-Oriented" engine where tokens behave like physical objects with real ownership semantics, making an entire class of DeFi exploits structurally impossible.

scrypto.title: Scrypto
scrypto.description: The smart-contract programming language built on Rust. Scrypto exposes Radix Engine's asset model directly so developers work with typed, safe resources instead of raw integer balances.

blueprints.title: Blueprints, Components & Royalties
blueprints.description: Developers write Blueprints (logic templates) that are instantiated as on-ledger Components. A unique protocol-level Developer Royalty system allows creators to earn a fee automatically every time their code is invoked by any dApp or user.

nft_catalog.title: Native Resource & NFT Catalog
nft_catalog.description: NFTs are first-class citizens on Radix: not an afterthought. The engine supports Mutable NFTs (attributes that evolve, ideal for games or identities) governed by a granular Role-Based Access Control system: mint, update, burn rules are set at protocol level, not in custom code.

defi.title: DeFi Layer
defi.subtitle: The Final Purpose
defi.description: The application layer that sits on top of all the layers below. Radix provides native, standardised DeFi building blocks that any developer can compose without re-implementing security from scratch.

native_defi.title: Native DeFi Components
native_defi.description: Liquidity pools, oracles, lending markets and decentralised exchanges (DEXs) built from standardised, audited Blueprints. Developers assemble DeFi products from proven pieces rather than writing everything from zero.

atomic_composability.title: Global Atomic Composability
atomic_composability.description: dApps can interact with each other simultaneously across any number of shards with full atomicity. One transaction can span a DEX swap, a lending deposit and an NFT mint: and either all succeed or none do.

interoperability.title: Interoperability & Bridges
interoperability.subtitle: The Doors to the Outside
interoperability.description: How the Radix ecosystem connects to the broader Web3 world: moving assets and messages between Radix and over 150 other blockchains.

hyperlane.title: Hyperlane
hyperlane.description: A decentralised, permissionless messaging infrastructure connecting Radix to 150+ blockchains (Ethereum, Solana, Arbitrum and more) for cross-chain message passing and liquidity bridging.

instabridge.title: Instabridge / Instapass
instabridge.description: The native Radix bridge and its optional compliance infrastructure (KYC/AML on-chain). Instapass enables institutional-grade, regulated DeFi access directly from the Radix ledger.

frontend.title: Authentication & Front-end
frontend.subtitle: The Web3 Plug
frontend.description: The tools that let web applications communicate with the Radix network. ROLA, the dApp Toolkit and human-readable Transaction Manifests together make building and using dApps safe and intuitive.

rola.title: ROLA (Radix Off-Ledger Authentication)
rola.description: A cryptographic protocol that lets users log in to dApps by proving they own a Radix account: without ever exposing a private key or seed phrase.

rdt.title: Radix dApp Toolkit (RDT)
rdt.description: Libraries and web components developers embed in their front-end UIs to handle wallet connection, transaction signing and account query flows with a few lines of code.

manifests.title: Transaction Manifests
manifests.description: Human-readable scripts that detail exactly which assets will enter and leave your account before you approve any transaction. No more blind-signing opaque hex blobs.

identity.title: User & Identity
identity.subtitle: Your Control Panel
identity.description: How end-users interact with the network. Radix Smart Accounts are smart contracts in themselves, enabling native multi-factor recovery and granular access rules without any additional setup.

smart_accounts.title: Smart Accounts (Native Account Abstraction)
smart_accounts.description: Every Radix wallet is a smart contract on-ledger, enabling complex recovery rules, multi-factor authentication (MFA) and programmable access control natively at the protocol level.

radix_wallet.title: Radix Wallet & Personas
radix_wallet.description: The official mobile app that acts as your vault and manages your digital identities (Personas). You decide exactly which personal attributes to share with each dApp: full self-sovereign identity.

radix_connect.title: Radix Connect
radix_connect.description: The WebRTC-based protocol that securely pairs your mobile phone with your desktop browser, letting you approve transactions from your phone while browsing dApps on your computer.

tooling.title: Data, APIs & Tooling
tooling.subtitle: The Workshop & Engine Room
tooling.description: The complete developer toolkit: from the public Testnet and local simulator to low-level institutional APIs and the public Gateway used by every dApp in the ecosystem.

stokenet.title: Stokenet
stokenet.description: The official public Testnet of Radix. It is an exact replica of Mainnet used by developers to safely test dApps and infrastructure before launching with real money.

resim.title: Radix Engine Simulator (resim)
resim.description: A command-line tool (CLI) and standalone local environment. Developers simulate the full Radix Engine on their own machines and run rapid Scrypto contract tests without any internet connection.

core_api.title: Core API & System API
core_api.description: Low-level direct programming interfaces used by institutional node operators and centralised exchanges (such as Bitfinex or KuCoin) to interact directly with the physical blockchain core and manage heavy transaction flows.

gateway.title: Gateway API / Network Gateway
gateway.description: The master indexing server that reads the entire blockchain (balances, histories, component states) and serves it to developers via an easy-to-use RESTful API: eliminating the costly need for every dApp to run and maintain its own node.

dashboard.title: Radix Dashboard
dashboard.description: The official block explorer: the visual interface. It translates the entire complex infrastructure of substates and components into a clean, readable web page so any user can audit the network, view transactions and check validator status.

infrastructure.title: Infrastructure | Run a Radix Node
infrastructure.description: Everything you need to run a Radix validator node: setup guides, hardware requirements, and monitoring.
